dossier.purpose: Local-first AI memory system. It mines project files and chat transcripts (Claude Code and Codex JSONL among others) into a 'palace' of wings > rooms > drawers stored verbatim in a vector store (ChromaDB by default; sqlite_exact, rust_exact, qdrant, milvus, pgvector are opt-in), searched with vector + BM25 hybrid ranking, plus a temporal SQLite knowledge graph, per-agent diaries and an append-only agent-coordination 'logstream' (README.md:26-37,286-306; mempalace/README.md:5-41). It is exposed as a CLI (`mempalace`), an MCP server (`mempalace-mcp`: 45 tools over stdio, optional HTTP hub; `mempalace-light-mcp`: 3 tools) and plugins/hooks for Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Antigravity, DeepSeek Harness and others (pyproject.toml:57-60; .claude-plugin/; .codex-plugin/). Ownership model on one host with several agents: one host-global palace by default (<config_dir>/palace; config_dir is ~/.mempalace for existing installs, otherwise ~/.config/mempalace: mempalace/config.py:255-275,918-935), scoped only by wing/room naming; each palace has one writer at a time (per-palace non-blocking flock; a long-lived MCP stdio server holds the lease after its first mutating call and peer servers become read-only for writes, unless a `mempalace serve` hub owns the palace and stdio servers/CLI/hooks proxy to it: mempalace/mcp_server/_guards.py:177-189,485-599; website/guide/shared-brain.md:19-20,43-63).

claims.claim: Tagline: 'Local-first AI memory. Verbatim storage, pluggable backend, 96.6% R@5 raw on LongMemEval — zero API calls.'

Stores conversation history as verbatim text and retrieves it with semantic search; 'does not summarize, extract, or paraphrase'; people/projects become wings, topics rooms, original content lives in drawers so searches can be scoped.
Retrieval layer is pluggable; default is ChromaDB; interface defined in mempalace/backends/base.py and alternative backends can be dropped in without touching the rest of the system.
'Nothing leaves your machine unless you opt in.'

Agent-guided setup: `npx skills add MemPalace/mempalace` installs three skills (mempalace, mempalace-recall, mempalace-task); installing a skill does not by itself install the CLI or MCP server, the setup skill guides those system changes and verifies the live connection.
Weekly stable-release checks are disabled by default, contact only PyPI when enabled, and never install updates automatically.
Direct CLI setup should use an isolated environment: `uv tool install mempalace` (recommended), `pipx install mempalace`, or pip inside an activated venv; then `mempalace init ~/projects/myapp`.

Docker image ghcr.io/mempalace/mempalace is multi-arch (amd64 + arm64); everything persists under /data; the first command needing embeddings downloads the model (~80 MB minilm, ~300 MB embeddinggemma) and needs network; the GPU image is not published (x86_64 only, build it yourself).

ChromaDB is the default backend and needs no configuration; every non-default backend is opt-in (sqlite_exact, rust_exact, milvus, qdrant, pgvector); select with --backend, MEMPALACE_BACKEND or config.json.
Quickstart: `mempalace mine ~/.claude/projects/ --mode convos` (scope with --wing per project), `mempalace search "..."`, `mempalace wake-up`.
45 MCP tools cover palace reads/writes, knowledge-graph operations, cross-wing navigation, drawer management, agent diaries, and agent coordination (logstream events + artifact handoffs).

Auto-save hooks for Claude Code, Codex CLI and Cursor IDE save periodically and before context compression; `mempalace sweep <transcript-dir>` stores one verbatim drawer per user/assistant message, idempotent and resume-safe.
'Claude Code sessions expire in 30 days without auto-save hooks wired' (links to a GitHub discussion and a retention checklist).

Requirements: Python 3.9+, a vector-store backend (ChromaDB default), ~300 MB for the embedding model; optional OpenAI-compatible remote embedding endpoint; no API key required for the core benchmark path.

install.command:
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install mempalace

install.method: Agent-guided setup (installs skills only; the agent then installs the CLI/MCP)
Docker (GHCR image; MCP over stdio, palace under /data)

docker pull ghcr.io/mempalace/mempalace:latest
docker run -i --rm -v mempalace-data:/data ghcr.io/mempalace/mempalace

claude plugin marketplace add MemPalace/mempalace
claude plugin install --scope user mempalace

codex plugin add mempalace@mempalace

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - CI test-linux on ubuntu-latest with Python 3.9/3.11/3.13 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:10-22); amd64 Docker image smoke-tested and published (.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:25-56,104-107); native wheel x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (.github/workflows/release-native.yml:24-26).
platforms.wsl2: unknown - no WSL2-specific install docs, CI job or test; the only WSL mention is incidental (CHANGELOG.md:125: a 4.99M-vector palace pushed WSL into swap).
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - CI test-macos on macos-latest, Python 3.13 (.github/workflows/ci.yml:46-55; the runner architecture is not pinned in the workflow); native wheel aarch64-apple-darwin (.github/workflows/release-native.yml:33-34); README says the Docker image 'runs natively on Apple Silicon' (README.md:110-112); Apple Silicon embeddinggemma/CoreML fix (CHANGELOG.md:154).
platforms.gpu: yes (optional, off by default) - extras `mempalace[gpu]` (onnxruntime-gpu/CUDA), `[dml]`, `[coreml]` (pyproject.toml:117-124); CPU is the default (website/guide/remote-server.md:115-118); Dockerfile.gpu is x86_64-only and not published (README.md:173-183); CI only build-checks it, no GPU runner (.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:118-138).

integrations.cli: Yes - `mempalace` console script (pyproject.toml:58; `python -m mempalace`: mempalace/__main__.py:3-5) with subcommands init, mine, sweep, sync, search, compress, wake-up, split, hook, instructions, rules, repair, repair-status, daemon, mcp, serve, migrate, migrate-wings, hallways, status, update, logstream, task, artifact, palace (mempalace/cli/parser.py:67-910; reference website/reference/cli.md). There is no CLI subcommand to delete a drawer (only `sync --apply` prunes drawers whose source files are gone: parser.py:265-294), none for export, backup or restore.
integrations.mcp: Yes - `mempalace-mcp` (pyproject.toml:59; mempalace/mcp_proxy.py:309-329): stdio by default, auto-proxies to a live local hub, exposes 45 tools (mempalace/mcp_server/schemas.py:9-980); `--transport http` and the turnkey `mempalace serve` give an HTTP hub with bearer token, TLS 1.2+, Host/Origin checks and `--read-only` (mempalace/mcp_server/_guards.py:21-70; mempalace/mcp_server/http.py:123-210; mempalace/cli/parser.py:550-579; website/guide/remote-server.md:120-160). `mempalace-light-mcp` is a 3-tool server (pyproject.toml:60; CHANGELOG.md:56). MCP protocol versions 2025-11-25 down to 2024-11-05 (mempalace/mcp_server/schemas.py:1016-1021); hand-rolled JSON-RPC, no `mcp` SDK dependency (pyproject.toml:29-50).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Python library only, no separate SDK package: documented imports mempalace.searcher.search_memories, mempalace.layers.MemoryStack, mempalace.knowledge_graph.KnowledgeGraph, mempalace.palace_graph, mempalace.dialect.Dialect (website/reference/python-api.md:5-120); a Hermes MemoryProvider adapter (mempalace/integrations/hermes/__init__.py:1-5). The only HTTP API is the MCP JSON-RPC endpoint /mcp plus /healthz, /statusz, /logstream/stream and /sync/peers on a hub (website/guide/shared-brain.md:495-518,556-558; website/guide/remote-server.md:205-211); no REST CRUD API and no non-Python SDK found.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: marketplace plugin .claude-plugin/ - plugin.json declares MCP server `mempalace-mcp` (.claude-plugin/plugin.json:10-14), hooks Stop/SessionEnd/PreCompact with 30/10/90 s timeouts calling `mempalace hook run --harness claude-code` (.claude-plugin/hooks/hooks.json:3-37; .claude-plugin/hooks/mempal-stop-hook.sh:24), 5 slash commands and 3 skills (.claude-plugin/README.md:32-54). Codex CLI: .codex-plugin/plugin.json + .agents/plugins/marketplace.json + root .mcp.json + root skills/ (manifest has mcpServers './.mcp.json' and NO hooks key, pinned by tests/test_codex_plugin_manifest.py:31-35; docs/RELEASING.md:36-42); .codex-plugin/hooks.json defines SessionStart/Stop/PreCompact calling `mempalace hook run --harness codex` (.codex-plugin/hooks.json:2-36; .codex-plugin/hooks/mempal-hook.sh:6) but is not referenced by the manifest; manual Codex hook wiring is documented in hooks/README.md:88-105 and website/guide/hooks.md:45-62. Manual MCP registration: `claude mcp add mempalace -- mempalace-mcp` / `codex mcp add mempalace -- mempalace-mcp` (mempalace/cli/cmd_serve.py:47-52; mempalace/instructions/init.md:64-68). Transcript readers: Claude Code JSONL (mempalace/normalize.py:301-360) and Codex rollout JSONL, event_msg user/agent messages only (mempalace/normalize.py:363-408; backfill `mempalace mine ~/.codex/sessions/ --mode convos`: hooks/README.md:242-245). Neither harness gets automatic session-start recall injection (hook_session_start returns {}: mempalace/hooks_cli.py:1504-1526; hooks/cursor/README.md:123). `mempalace task launch --runner codex|claude` can spawn `codex exec`/`claude --print` from a stored task (mempalace/cli/cmd_coord.py:497-508).

readme.telemetry_and_network: Docs state no telemetry/phone-home (CLAUDE.md:27,34; website/guide/remote-server.md:15-19; README.md:39). Code: no analytics/telemetry client in mempalace/ (grep for telemetry/posthog/analytics/sentry hits only comments: mempalace/__init__.py:59-63, mempalace/mcp_server/__init__.py:37-45). The repo never sets ChromaDB's anonymized_telemetry (no Settings(...)/ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY anywhere; clients are plain chromadb.PersistentClient(path=...): mempalace/backends/chroma.py:3088,3198); mempalace/__init__.py:59-63 only lowers a chromadb posthog logger's level and asserts chromadb 1.x's posthog client is a no-op stub, which cannot be confirmed from this repo (uv.lock pins chromadb 1.5.7 at uv.lock:531-533 and lists no posthog package). Network calls found in code: (a) PyPI release check to https://pypi.org/pypi/mempalace/json - opt-in, default off, `mempalace update check` forces one (mempalace/update_awareness.py:85-96,143-147; website/reference/cli.md:7-19); (b) Wikipedia REST lookup only with allow_network=True, default False (mempalace/entity_registry.py:177-193,556-590); (c) LLM-assisted `mempalace init` is on by default but targets local Ollama (http://localhost:11434) with fallback to heuristics; external providers need explicit selection and a consent prompt when the key comes from the environment (mempalace/cli/cmd_init.py:31-108; mempalace/llm_client.py:1-22); (d) optional OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint (mempalace/embedding.py:24-33; README.md:335) and optional networked backends qdrant/milvus/pgvector that receive verbatim text when pointed at remote services (website/guide/configuration.md:44-49); (e) hub/peer HTTP between MemPalace processes on loopback or user-configured peers with bearer tokens (mempalace/mcp_proxy.py:101-116; mempalace/transport.py:96-100; website/guide/shared-brain.md:82-97,527-558). Required downloads on first use: default minilm model from ChromaDB's S3 (~80 MB) and, if selected, onnx-community/embeddinggemma-300m-ONNX from Hugging Face (~300 MB) (README.md:133-136; Dockerfile:75-80; mempalace/embedding.py:267,427-438). No account or API key is required for the core path (README.md:337). Separate from the package, the docs site build can embed Google Analytics when MEMPALACE_DOCS_GA_ID is set (website/.vitepress/config.mts:14,33-34; .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml:47).

code.architecture: Python package mempalace/: cli/ (argparse parser + cmd_* handlers), mcp_server/ (hand-written JSON-RPC server, stdio + HTTP; tools_read/tools_write/tools_kg/tools_diary/tools_coord, schemas.py, protocol.py, _guards.py gates), mcp_proxy.py (stdio->hub proxy), hooks_cli.py (session hooks), miner.py (project files) and convo_miner.py + normalize.py (transcripts: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, ChatGPT, Slack...), sweeper.py (per-message miner, Claude Code JSONL only), searcher/ (vector + BM25 hybrid ranking, closet boost), palace/ (collection access, closets, per-palace flock mine_lock/palace_lock), backends/ (base.py contract + chroma, sqlite_exact, rust_exact, qdrant, milvus, pgvector), knowledge_graph.py (SQLite temporal triples; default DB ~/.mempalace/knowledge_graph.sqlite3 unless --palace is given: knowledge_graph.py:49, mcp_server/_guards.py:937-940), logstream.py/logsync.py/replica.py (append-only agent events and artifacts in logstream.sqlite3, multi-master peer sync), wal.py (JSONL write audit log), repair.py/migrate.py/backups.py (index rebuild and backups), daemon.py/service.py (opt-in write queue), embedding.py (minilm default, embeddinggemma, openai-compat; ONNX providers), config.py (env > config.json > defaults), dialect.py (lossy AAAK summaries), update_awareness.py. The big packages mcp_server, cli, palace and searcher are 'fragment' packages whose files are exec()'d into one shared namespace (mempalace/mcp_server/__init__.py:145-169; mempalace/cli/__init__.py:83-106; mempalace/palace/__init__.py:95-113). Data at rest: <config_dir>/palace/ (chroma.sqlite3 + HNSW segments, drawers and closets collections), logstream.sqlite3 in the palace dir, <config_dir>/wal/write_log.jsonl (mempalace/wal.py:24), ~/.mempalace/hook_state/ (hook.log, per-session markers: hooks_cli.py:39-40), ~/.mempalace/locks/ (palace/palace_lock.py:240-245), ~/.mempalace/server/ (hub token/serverinfo). Rust crates are an optional exact-vector accelerator sharing sqlite_exact.sqlite3 (crates/README.md:1-15).
code.packaging_and_release: Python: hatchling sdist + wheel of package `mempalace` only (pyproject.toml:159-164; hooks/*.sh and plugin directories are not in the wheel). Release flow (docs/RELEASING.md:64-113): publishing a GitHub Release triggers .github/workflows/publish.yml, which validates the tag shape, requires the tagged commit to be an ancestor of main, requires tag == mempalace/version.py, builds with `python -m build` and uploads with pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish via PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no stored token) behind a manual-approval `pypi` environment (publish.yml:3-25,46-51,84-124). No checksum, signature or attestation step is configured in that workflow (whether PEP 740 attestations are produced would be the pinned action's default; not verified here). Docker: .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml smoke-tests the amd64 image (CLI mine+search, MCP stdio handshake, compose config), then pushes multi-arch amd64+arm64 images to ghcr.io/mempalace/mempalace on main and v* tags with `provenance: mode=max` and `sbom: true` (docker-publish.yml:19-24,58-116); the GPU image is build-checked only. Native: .github/workflows/release-native.yml builds PyO3 wheels (linux x86_64/aarch64, windows x86_64, macOS x86_64/aarch64) and `mempalace-native` executables (linux/windows/macOS) and attaches them to the GitHub release with `gh release upload`; no checksums/signatures, and wheels are distributed outside PyPI (release-native.yml:18-106; crates/README.md:17-23). .github/workflows/version-guard.yml enforces that 7 version sources agree (version-guard.yml:23-85). Claude/Codex plugins are distributed straight from the git repo through marketplace manifests (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json; .agents/plugins/marketplace.json), not as artifacts. Active workflows pin third-party actions by commit SHA.
code.tests_and_ci: pytest (+pytest-cov, hypothesis, pytest-rerunfailures; pyproject.toml:77-103,210-238). tests/ has ~190 Python test modules (171 top-level, 8 in tests/mcp/, 11 in tests/benchmarks/ which CI excludes) with ~4,950 `def test_` functions in total, plus helpers/conftest; Rust tests in crates (10 #[test]/cfg(test) hits: crates/mempalace-core/src/lib.rs, crates/mempalace-cli/tests/search.rs); 4 Node test files for the DSH plugin (.dsh-plugin/test/*.test.mjs, driven by tests/test_dsh_plugin.py). Project self-checks include manifest/hook tests (tests/test_codex_plugin_manifest.py, tests/test_claude_plugin_hook_config.py, tests/test_hooks_cli.py) and README-vs-code claim tests (tests/test_readme_claims.py). CI .github/workflows/ci.yml (push/PR to main and develop): test-linux (Python 3.9/3.11/3.13), test-windows (3.13, with reruns for known ChromaDB HNSW flakes), test-macos (3.13), lint (ruff check + ruff format --check, ruff==0.16.6), test-rust (cargo fmt/check/test on linux/windows/macOS, builds the native wheel and runs backend suites with MEMPALACE_REQUIRE_NATIVE=1); pytest runs with --ignore=tests/benchmarks and --cov-fail-under=80 (pyproject.toml:233 says 85). Other workflows: version-guard.yml, docker-publish.yml, release-native.yml, publish.yml, deploy-docs.yml (VitePress -> GitHub Pages); bump-plugin-version.yml.disabled is inactive. No CodeQL/dependency-audit workflow; dependabot covers pip and github-actions only (.github/dependabot.yml:1-12); mypy is a dev dependency but not gated (pyproject.toml:97-102). I did not run any tests or benchmarks.

Optional extras: dev 8 (pytest, pytest-cov, pytest-rerunfailures, ruff==0.16.6, psutil, hypothesis, pre-commit, mypy), spellcheck 1, milvus 2, pgvector 1, gpu 1, dml 1, coreml 1, extract 2 (striprtf, markitdown[docx,pdf,pptx,xlsx] on py>=3.10), multilingual 0 (empty alias) (pyproject.toml:76-142); [dependency-groups].dev 8 (pyproject.toml:144-157). uv.lock (committed; used by the Dockerfile) locks 182 packages including chromadb 1.5.7, whose declared dependencies include grpcio, kubernetes, onnxruntime, opentelemetry-*, httpx, uvicorn, pydantic (uv.lock:531-574). claim_checks.evidence: Content-carrying egress paths found in code are opt-in: PyPI check off by default (mempalace/update_awareness.py:143-147), Wikipedia lookup needs allow_network=True (mempalace/entity_registry.py:556-590), external LLM providers need explicit selection plus a consent prompt for environment keys (mempalace/cli/cmd_init.py:31-108), remote embeddings/backends are explicit config (mempalace/embedding.py:24-33; website/guide/configuration.md:44-49). Release-note performance/memory measurements on large palaces and proxied MCP sessions (167k-drawer sqlite_exact palace; stdio session behind a hub). No figures are published for the native rust_exact engine.
benchmarks.value: mempalace_status 6997 ms -> 1045 ms; warm mempalace_search 6364 ms -> 210-1600 ms (3.8.0); proxied stdio session ~17 MB vs ~80 MB import weight; native engine: none published

risks: One host, several agents, single writer: the palace is guarded by a non-blocking per-palace flock; an MCP stdio server takes the writer lease for its lifetime on its first mutating call, a second harness's `mempalace-mcp` then gets -32001 'Peer MCP writer active' for writes, and CLI/hook mines get MineAlreadyRunning unless a `mempalace serve` hub owns the palace and everything proxies to it (mempalace/mcp_server/_guards.py:177-189,485-599; mempalace/palace/palace_lock.py:207-296; website/guide/shared-brain.md:43-63; website/guide/remote-server.md:194-204). Per-session stdio servers also exit after 8 h idle by default (_guards.py:113-115).

Deletion and recovery are thin: mempalace_delete_drawer and delete_by_source are described as irreversible (mempalace/mcp_server/schemas.py:437-438,503-504); the write-ahead log redacts content keys, so deleted text cannot be replayed from it (mempalace/wal.py:28-30,84-96; tools_write.py:516-524) and bulk `mine` writes are not WAL-logged at all (_wal_log is called only from tools_write/tools_diary/tools_kg/sync.py); there is no soft-delete/restore, no backup/restore/export/delete CLI (mempalace/cli/parser.py:67-910; mempalace/exporter.py:68 is not wired to CLI or MCP), no wing/room-level or KG-fact deletion (KG facts can only be invalidated: mempalace/knowledge_graph.py:343-375; logstream is append-only: website/guide/shared-brain.md:458-460). Backups exist only as side effects of repair/migrate: legacy `repair` keeps one rolling <palace>.backup that it deletes and rewrites each run (mempalace/cli/cmd_repair.py:287-298), `migrate` keeps at most max_backups=10 (mempalace/config.py:1546-1573). The project's own recovery guidance is rebuild-from-SQLite and warns that re-mining drops MCP-added and diary-only drawers (integrations/shared/recall-protocol.md:86-107).

Durability rests on ChromaDB HNSW + SQLite/FTS5, with a visible history of index damage: release notes record index divergence, FTS5 corruption, stale-index handling and a 'silent write-loss path' closed in 3.10.0 (CHANGELOG.md:15,85,89-90). The server refuses all non-allowlisted tools with -32002 when the SQLite quick_check fails (mempalace/mcp_server/_guards.py:884-922), refuses writes with -32005 after an in-place package upgrade until the server is restarted (mempalace/mcp_server/protocol.py:567-617), and falls back to BM25-only search when the vector index diverges (_guards.py:1166-1218); repair is a manual CLI step (website/reference/cli.md:143-164).

Codex integration is thinner than Claude Code's: the Codex plugin manifest registers MCP + skills but no hooks (tests/test_codex_plugin_manifest.py:31-35), no SessionEnd for Codex (hooks/README.md:107-112), `mempalace sweep` parses only Claude Code JSONL (mempalace/sweeper.py:89-151), the Codex transcript parser keeps only event_msg user/agent text, not tool output (mempalace/normalize.py:363-408), and neither harness gets automatic session-start recall injection (mempalace/hooks_cli.py:1504-1526). Project-wing derivation reads a top-level `cwd` (hooks_cli.py:1273-1315) while the repo's Codex fixtures put identifiers under `payload` (tests/test_codex_fallback.py:16-19), so Codex behavior there is unverified in the repo. The Codex manifest still advertises 44 tools (.codex-plugin/plugin.json:4).

Scoping is convention-based and differs by capture path: one host-global palace by default (mempalace/config.py:918-935); hook-driven transcript mines always use wing `sessions` (mempalace/hooks_cli.py:1185-1197) while checkpoint diary entries go to wing_<project> under agent `claude` or `codex` (hooks_cli.py:1211-1222,1453-1465) and the legacy shell hook mines the transcript's parent directory with no wing, which resolves to wing_api (hooks/mempal_save_hook.sh:268-269; mempalace/convo_miner.py:850-872). Search/list filters are wing, room, exact source_file and dates, with no agent filter (mempalace/mcp_server/schemas.py:286-348,550-579). State is split between the config dir and legacy ~/.mempalace even on XDG installs: hook state, locks and the default KG database (hooks_cli.py:39-40; mempalace/palace/mine_lock.py:31; mempalace/knowledge_graph.py:49).

Capture is unredacted and unencrypted: hooks mine whole transcripts including tool output verbatim; grep of miner.py, convo_miner.py, normalize.py and hooks_cli.py finds no secret/credential scrubbing and no at-rest encryption code exists in mempalace/ (only advice not to file secrets: website/guide/shared-brain.md:154-155). A loopback hub is tokenless unless a token is set (website/guide/shared-brain.md:82-90).

Network/footprint unknowns: the repo does not set ChromaDB's own telemetry flag (see telemetry notes); first embedding use needs network to fetch a ~80 MB (ChromaDB S3) or ~300 MB (Hugging Face) model (README.md:133-136; mempalace/embedding.py:267,427-438) and the repo does not state the license of those downloaded model weights; the dependency graph is heavy (chromadb pulls grpcio, kubernetes, onnxruntime, opentelemetry; 182 locked packages: uv.lock:535-574) and an unproxied stdio session imports ~77 MB per agent process (mempalace/mcp_proxy.py:1-20).

Maintenance and scope: 18 changelog releases between 3.0.0 (2026-04-06) and 3.10.0 (2026-09-15), with behavior changes inside minors (CHANGELOG.md:13-22,852); .github/CODEOWNERS names two owners (:5-6). Docs lag code: ROADMAP.md still describes v3.1.1/v4.0.0-alpha (ROADMAP.md:3,25); website/guide/hooks.md describes a blocking-hook flow (:9-12) while the default is silent save; website/guide/getting-started.md:25 says chromadb>=0.5.0 vs chromadb>=1.5.4,<2 (pyproject.toml:30); mempalace/README.md:16 still says AAAK is '30x lossless' though dialect.py:12-15 and docs/HISTORY.md:94-99 say it is lossy; docs still point at ~/.mempalace although new installs use ~/.config/mempalace (CHANGELOG.md:22; website/guide/configuration.md:5-18). Scope reaches well beyond memory: agent task coordination and headless launch of codex/claude (mempalace/cli/cmd_coord.py:497-508), peer replication, six storage backends and a Rust engine.

checks.note: Every citation matches. Claude plugin: plugin.json:10-14 maps mempalace to mempalace-mcp. hooks.json registers Stop 30 s, SessionEnd 10 s and PreCompact 90 s. The Stop and PreCompact wrappers call `--harness claude-code` (line 24 of each); SessionEnd backgrounds the same call with claude-code as the default (session-end-hook.sh:38).
